questions.stem:
Figure 1 shows the speed-time graph of a cyclist moving on a straight road over a 7 s period. The sections of the graph from $t=0$ to $t=3$, and from $t=3$ to $t=7$, are straight lines. The section from $t=3$ to $t=7$ is parallel to the $t$-axis.

State what can be deduced about the motion of the cyclist from the fact that

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) the graph from $t=0$ to $t=3$ is a straight line,
(1)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) B1: Constant acceleration
(1)
Accept 'steady' instead of 'constant'. Allow o.e. within reason! But must have idea of constant. 'constant speed and constant acceleration' for (a) or (b) is B0

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) the graph from $t=3$ to $t=7$ is parallel to the $t$-axis.
(1)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) B1: Constant speed/velocity
(1)
Accept 'steady' instead of 'constant'. Allow o.e. within reason! But must have idea of constant. 'constant speed and constant acceleration' for (a) or (b) is B0

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Find the distance travelled by the cyclist during this 7 s period.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) Distance $= \frac{1}{2}(2+5) \times 3, + (4 \times 5)$
$= 30.5$ m
M1 A1, B1, A1
(4)
M1 for valid attempt at area of this trap. as area of a trap. Or this trap. as = triangle + rectangle, i.e. correct formula used with at most a slip in numbers.
B1 for area of rectangle as $5 \times 4$
Treating whole as a single const acceln situation, or whole as a single trapezium, is M0.
If assume that top speed is 5.1 or 5.2, allow full marks on f.t. basis (but must be consistent)

questions.stem: A train moves along a straight track with constant acceleration. Three telegraph poles are set at equal intervals beside the track at points $A$, $B$ and $C$, where $AB = 50$ m and $BC = 50$ m. The front of the train passes $A$ with speed $22.5\,\mathrm{m\,s}^{-1}$, and 2 s later it passes $B$. Find

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) the acceleration of the train,
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) $AB$: $50 = 2 \times 22.5 + \frac{1}{2}a.4$
$\Rightarrow a = 2.5\,\mathrm{m\,s}^{-2}$
M1 A1, A1
(3)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) the speed of the front of the train when it passes $C$,
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) $v^2 = 22.5^2 + 2 \times 2.5 \times 100$
$\Rightarrow v \approx 31.7(2)\,\mathrm{m\,s}^{-1}$
M1 A1ft, A1
(3)
M1 for valid use of data (e.g. finding speed at $B$ by spurious means and using this to get $v$ at $C$ is M0).
Accept answer as AWRT 31.7
In (b) and (c), f.t. A marks are for f.t. on wrong $a$ and/or answer from (b).

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) the time that elapses from the instant the front of the train passes $B$ to the instant it passes $C$.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) $v_B = 22.5 + 2 \times 2.5 = 27.5$ (must be used)
$31.72 = 27.5 + 2.5t$ OR $50 = 27.5t + \frac{1}{2} \times 2.5t^2$ OR $50 = \frac{1}{2}(27.5+31.72)t$
$\Rightarrow t \approx 1.69$ s
M1, M1 A1ft, A1
(4)
OR $31.72 = 22.5 + 2.5T$ OR $100 = 22.5t + \frac{1}{2} \times 2.5T^2$
$\Rightarrow T \approx 3.69$
$\Rightarrow t \approx 3.69 - 2 = 1.69$ s
M1 A1ft, M1 A1
(4)
OR $50 = 31.7t - \frac{1}{2} \times 2.5t^2$
Solve quadratic to get $t = 1.69$ s
M2 A1ft, A1
(4)
NB note slight changes to scheme: dependency now in (c) and new rule on accuracy of answers.
M1 + M1 to get to an equation in the required $t$ (normally two stages, but they can do it in one via 3rd alternative above)
Ans is cao. Hence premature approx (-> e.g. 1.68) is A0.
But if they use a 3 sf answer from (b) and then give answer to (c) as 1.7, allow full marks. And accept 2 or 3 s.f. answer or better to (c).

questions.stem: A particle $P$ of mass 0.5 kg is on a rough plane inclined at an angle $\alpha$ to the horizontal, where $\tan\alpha = \frac{3}{4}$. The particle is held at rest on the plane by the action of a force of magnitude 4 N acting up the plane in a direction parallel to a line of greatest slope of the plane, as shown in Figure 2. The particle is on the point of slipping up the plane.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the coefficient of friction between $P$ and the plane.
(7)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) $R = 0.5g\cos\alpha = 0.4g$
$4 = F + 0.5g\sin\alpha$
$F = \mu R$ used
$4 = 0.4g.\mu + 0.3g$
$\Rightarrow \mu \approx 0.27(0)$
M1 A1, M1 A1, M1, M1 A1
(7)
1st two M1's require correct number of the correct terms, with valid attempt to resolve the correct relevant term (valid 'resolve' = $\times \sin/\cos$).
4th M1 (dept) for forming equn in $\mu$ + numbers only

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The force of magnitude 4 N is removed.
(b) Find the acceleration of $P$ down the plane.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) $0.5a = 0.3g - 0.27 \times 0.4g$
$\Rightarrow a \approx (+)3.76\,\mathrm{m\,s}^{-2}$ (or 3.8)
M1 A2,1,0ft, A1
(4)
A marks: f.t. on their $R$, $F$ etc. Deduct one A mark (up to 2) for each wrong term. (Note slight change from original scheme)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- In first equn, allow their $R$ or $F$ in the equation for full marks.

questions.stem:
A steel girder $AB$ has weight 210 N. It is held in equilibrium in a horizontal position by two vertical cables. One cable is attached to the end $A$. The other cable is attached to the point $C$ on the girder, where $AC = 90$ cm, as shown in Figure 3. The girder is modelled as a uniform rod, and the cables as light inextensible strings.

Given that the tension in the cable at $C$ is twice the tension in the cable at $A$, find

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) the tension in the cable at $A$,
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) $R + 2R = 210 \Rightarrow R = 70$ N
M1 A1
(2)
M1 for a valid method to get $R$ (almost always resolving!)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) show that $AB = 120$ cm.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) e.g. M($A$): $140 \times 90 = 210 \times d$
$\Rightarrow d = 60 \Rightarrow AB = 120$ cm
M1 A1ft, M1 A1
(4)
1st M1 for a valid moments equation
2nd M1 for complete solution to find $AB$ (or verification)
Allow 'verification', e.g. showing $140 \times 90 = 210 \times 60$ M1 A1
$1260 = 1260$ QED M1 A1
Note that they can take moments legitimately about many points

parts.label: c
parts.text:
A small load of weight $W$ newtons is attached to the girder at $B$. The load is modelled as a particle. The girder remains in equilibrium in a horizontal position. The tension in the cable at $C$ is now three times the tension in the cable at $A$.
(c) Find the value of $W$.
(7)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) $4S = 210 + W$
e.g. M($B$): $S \times 120 + 3S \times 30 = 210 \times 60$
Solve $\to (S=60$ and$) W = 30$
M1 A1, M1 A2,1,0, M1 A1
(7)
In both equations, allow whatever they think $S$ is in their equations for full marks (e.g. if using $S=70$).
2nd M1 A2 is for a moments equation (which may be about any one of 4+ points!)
1st M1 A1 is for a second equation (resolving or moments)
If they have two moments equations, given M1 A2 if possible for the best one
2 M marks only available without using $S = 70$.
If take mass as 210 (hence use $210g$) consistently: treat as MR, i.e. deduct up to two A marks and treat rest as f.t. (Answers all as given = 9.8). But allow full marks in (b) ($g$'s should all cancel and give correct result).

questions.stem: A car is towing a trailer along a straight horizontal road by means of a horizontal tow-rope. The mass of the car is 1400 kg. The mass of the trailer is 700 kg. The car and the trailer are modelled as particles and the tow-rope as a light inextensible string. The resistances to motion of the car and the trailer are assumed to be constant and of magnitude 630 N and 280 N respectively. The driving force on the car, due to its engine, is 2380 N. Find

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) the acceleration of the car,
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) Car + trailer: $2100a = 2380 - 280 - 630$
$= 1470 \Rightarrow a = 0.7\,\mathrm{m\,s}^{-2}$
M1 A1, A1
(3)
M1 for a complete (potential) valid method to get $a$

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) the tension in the tow-rope.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) e.g. trailer: $700 \times 0.7 = T - 280$
$\Rightarrow T = 770$ N
M1 A1ft, A1
(3)
If consider car: then get $1400a = 2380 - 630 - T$.
Allow M1 A1 for equn of motion for car or trailer wherever seen (e.g. in (a)).
So if consider two separately in (a), can get M1 A1 from (b) for one equation; then M1 A1 from (a) for second equation, and then A1 [(a)] for $a$ and A1 [(b)] for $T$.
In equations of motion, M1 requires no missing or extra terms and dimensionally correct (e.g. extra force, or missing mass, is M0). If unclear which body is being considered, assume that the body is determined by the mass used. Hence if '$1400a$' used, assume it is the car and mark forces etc accordingly. But allow e.g. 630/280 confused as an A error.

parts.label: c
parts.text:
When the car and trailer are moving at $12\,\mathrm{m\,s}^{-1}$, the tow-rope breaks. Assuming that the driving force on the car and the resistances to motion are unchanged,
(c) find the distance moved by the car in the first 4 s after the tow-rope breaks.
(6)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) Car: $1400a' = 2380 - 630$
$\Rightarrow a' = 1.25\,\mathrm{m\,s}^{-2}$
distance $= 12 \times 4 + \frac{1}{2} \times 1.25 \times 4^2$
$= 58$ m
M1 A1, A1, M1 A1ft, A1
(6)
Must be finding a new acceleration here. (If they get 1.25 erroneously in (a), and then simply assume it is the same acceln here, it is M0).

parts.label: d
parts.text:
(d) State how you have used the modelling assumption that the tow-rope is inextensible.
(1)
parts.mark_scheme:
(d) Same acceleration for car and trailer
B1
(1)
Allow o.e. but you must be convinced they are saying that it is same acceleration for both bodies. E.g. 'acceleration constant' on its own is B0. Ignore extras, but 'acceleration and tension same at $A$ and $B$' is B0.

questions.stem:
[In this question the unit vectors $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$ are due east and north respectively]

A ship $S$ is moving with constant velocity $(-2.5\mathbf{i}+6\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{km\,h}^{-1}$. At time 1200, the position vector of $S$ relative to a fixed origin $O$ is $(16\mathbf{i}+5\mathbf{j})$ km. Find

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) the speed of $S$,
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) Speed $= \sqrt{2.5^2+6^2} = 6.5\,\mathrm{km\,h}^{-1}$
M1 A1
(2)
M1 needs square, add and $\surd$ correct components

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) the bearing on which $S$ is moving.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) Bearing $= 360 - \arctan(2.5/6) \approx 337$
M1 A1
(2)
M1 for finding acute angle $= \arctan(2.5/6)$ or $\arctan(6/2.5)$ (i.e. $67°/23°$). Accept answer as AWRT 337.

parts.label: c
parts.text:
The ship is heading directly towards a submerged rock $R$. A radar tracking station calculates that, if $S$ continues on the same course with the same speed, it will hit $R$ at the time 1500.
(c) Find the position vector of $R$.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) $\mathbf{R} = (16 - 3\times2.5)\mathbf{i} + (5+3\times6)\mathbf{j}$
$= 8.5\mathbf{i}+23\mathbf{j}$
M1, A1
(2)
M1 needs non-zero initial p.v. used + 'their 3' $\times$ velocity vector

parts.label: d
parts.text:
The tracking station warns the ship's captain of the situation. The captain maintains $S$ on its course with the same speed until the time is 1400. He then changes course so that $S$ moves due north at a constant speed of $5\,\mathrm{km\,h}^{-1}$. Assuming that $S$ continues to move with this new constant velocity, find
(d) an expression for the position vector of the ship $t$ hours after 1400,
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(d) At 1400 $\mathbf{s} = 11\mathbf{i}+17\mathbf{j}$
At time $t$, $\mathbf{s} = 11\mathbf{i}+(17+5t)\mathbf{j}$
M1 A1, M1 A1
(4)
Allow 1st M1 even if non-zero initial p.v. not used here

parts.label: e
parts.text:
(e) the time when $S$ will be due east of $R$,
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(e) East of $R \Rightarrow 17+5t = 23$
$\Rightarrow t = 6/5 \Rightarrow 1512$ hours
M1, A1
(2)
A1 is for answer as a time of the day

parts.label: f
parts.text:
(f) the distance of $S$ from $R$ at the time 1600.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(f) At 1600 $\mathbf{s} = 11\mathbf{i}+27\mathbf{j}$
$\mathbf{s}-\mathbf{r} = 2.5\mathbf{i}+4\mathbf{j}$
Distance $= \sqrt{2.5^2+4^2} \approx 4.72$ km
M1, M1 A1
(3)
1st M1 for using $t = 2$ or $4$ (but not 200, 400, 6, 16 etc) and forming $\mathbf{s}-\mathbf{r}$ or $\mathbf{r}-\mathbf{s}$
